references.text: The parallel text in Matthew where Judas goes to the chief priests and asks what they will give him to betray Jesus. Both Matthew and Luke describe Judas' initiative to seek out the religious leaders to arrange the handing over of Jesus ([ref:Matt 26:14-16|Matthew 26:14-16]).

The parallel text in Mark where Judas Iscariot goes to the chief priests to betray Jesus to them. Mark uses the same pattern: Judas actively seeks out the leaders to hand over Jesus ([ref:Mark 14:10-11|Mark 14:10-11]).

Later in the same chapter, Jesus mentions that the chief priests and "strategoi" (the commander of the temple guard) are among those who come to arrest him. This shows that the same groups Judas negotiated with in verse 4 were the ones who carried out the arrest ([ref:Luk 22:52|Luke 22:52]).

John describes how Judas comes with a detachment of soldiers and guards from the chief priests and Pharisees to arrest Jesus – the practical execution of what Judas arranged with the leaders in Luke 22:4 ([ref:Joh 18:3-5|John 18:3-5]).

John explains that the devil had already put it into the heart of Judas Iscariot to betray Jesus, which provides the spiritual background for Judas' action in seeking out the chief priests ([ref:Joh 13:2|John 13:2]).
The preceding verse explains that Satan entered Judas, which motivated him to go to the chief priests and the leaders of the temple guard as described in verse 4 ([ref:Luk 22:3|Luke 22:3]).

The commander of the temple guard (στρατηγός) is also mentioned in Acts as one who confronts the apostles. This title "strategoi" in Luke 22:4 points to the military leadership of the temple guard, which played a key role in the arrest of Jesus ([ref:Apg 4:1|Acts 4:1]).

Peter's speech about Judas as the "guide for those who seized Jesus" confirms that Judas actively planned and cooperated with the religious authorities, as seen in Luke 22:4 ([ref:Apg 1:16-17|Acts 1:16-17]).

The messianic psalm speaks prophetically about a close friend who betrays: "Even my close friend, someone I trusted, one who shared my bread, has turned against me." This is an Old Testament background for Judas' betrayal ([ref:Sal 41:10|Psalm 41:10]).
